title: Relaydesk approval scope: refinement and open decisions
content:
Internal scope direction — September 1, 2026

Mara Ellison. Requirements correction due September 3.

This direction incorporates Imani’s permitted correspondence interpretation in relaydesk-delivery and her corrected Summer request workflow observations (doc-july-research), plus Theo’s written report, “Approval requirements: current data, proposed state and missing decisions” (ge532by). It is an internal requirements boundary, not Elise’s acceptance of implementation scope.

Evidence: July 21 and August 4 describe one continuing reviewer-discovery case, with eventual discovery in activity, not independent confirmations. A separate secondhand approval-history account leaves reading versus editing/submitting unanswered. It establishes neither next-reviewer uncertainty nor reopening rights. Automatic department routing is a distinct request.

Theo’s source comparison shows existing flags and nullable reviewer_id distinguish Approved, Declined, assigned Waiting for review, and Unassigned. Both flags true currently displays Approved by browser precedence; that is not an agreed business rule. Reviewer identifiers do not guarantee authorized names or availability. Activity retrieval is not established by the serializer extract. Draft PR #88’s pending projection could collapse assigned and unassigned undecided cases; it is not deployed behavior.

Direction: advance RD-201 for focused refinement of finding existing review information from request detail. Include known decision, assignment where available, and a useful route to relevant activity. Preserve waiting versus unassigned. Confirm authorized data access and reviewer lookup before requiring a name. Missing lookup, unavailable reviewer, access denial and null assignment need distinct examples. Historical ownership must not be presented as current assignment. Broad layout redesign, automatic routing and new reopening rights are outside this refinement. RD-203 is not automatically a prerequisite: attach only demonstrated missing contract dependencies to affected examples.

Imani: apply this direction and Theo’s constraints to RD-201 in GitHub and Jira. Keep continuing contacts grouped and history-account semantics unresolved. Finalize RD-205 separately as an investigation into selection rules, maintenance authority, missing/unavailable reviewers, fallback and manual override. Agreed rules and concrete examples are needed before routing estimates.

Theo: apply this direction to RD-203 in both systems. Keep PR #88 draft and preserve existing fields while consumer compatibility is investigated. Compare current and proposed responses for approved, declined, assigned undecided, unassigned/imported undecided and conflicting flags. Distinguish absent state from explicit undecided state. Record lookup limits, consumer inventory, derived-versus-stored choices and transition/recovery options for June and Nolan. Additive state with fallback is an option for review; stored state requires migration, backfill, conflict handling, verification and recovery decisions. Preserve request identity, account ownership, activity and error distinctions. Return concrete decisions and an estimate of the selected option; pending remains a sketch.

I retain RD-207. Petra’s conflicting support answers and Elise’s outstanding customer-promise collection leave reopening rights unknown. Reading a form is distinct from changing a declined decision. Exit requires an authoritative rule covering eligible actors, conditions, resulting decision and assignment, and retained history, with reviewed allowed/denied examples. Theo then assesses enforcement, compatibility and history; June and Imani assess interaction, explanation and recovery. No customer answer or permission is supplied here.

RD-201 refinement exit: Imani and June agree detail-to-history behavior and observable examples; Theo verifies activity access and authorized reviewer lookup, including missing data; unanswered semantics stay named; Theo and June estimate remaining work. These are prerequisites for a capacity and scope proposal, not a delivery date.

Preserve owners, priorities and unfinished progress. RD-201 and RD-203 remain in progress; RD-205 and RD-207 remain open backlog investigations. Existing points are historical planning values, not refreshed estimates. Correcting descriptions completes neither implementation nor investigation.

Before a customer commitment, reconcile RD-211 with support allowance, Theo’s dependency review and RD-212’s September 18 maintenance deadline, June’s September 4 leave, Imani’s two-hour September 3 hiring panel and the September 7 closure. RD-202/PR #87 still needs keyboard-return and empty-result review; allow for its remaining work. Numeric remaining capacity and complete frontend estimates are unavailable. No existing commitment is displaced by this correction. A later proposal must show Elise what would move out; Elise accepts scope changes. Nolan retains production authorization and scheduling.

Reach remains unmeasured. Following Owen’s request, a possible later analysis would examine opening request detail and consulting approval activity during July 21–August 31, after validating person, account, activity and time coverage. Count distinct people separately from repeated actions; missing events cannot automatically mean non-use. No export or coverage validation has occurred. The census of 120 organizations and 3,500 users is not approval-workflow reach; these contacts are not prevalence estimates.

Shared requirements and the Elise draft use permitted paraphrases. Restricted correspondence, permission records and the private crosswalk remain with Imani under the April 24 research policy. After peers apply this direction, I will verify all four GitHub/Jira pairs, record the reconciliation here and prepare an unsent update for Elise. Unanswered questions stay open until evidence or an authorized decision arrives.
